briefings.headline: Be ready for Blanco’s changeup; attack strikes you can drive
briefings.message: Ronel Blanco is the high-confidence predicted starter. His overall results and handedness splits are small samples. Hunt fastballs and breaking balls when you get them, but stay selective against the changeup: it has a 43.3% whiff rate and .182 xwOBA allowed. Brandon Nimmo, sit on breaking balls; Wyatt Langford and Justin Foscue, look for fastballs. Make Blanco prove the changeup is working.
reminders: Blanco’s left-handed and right-handed split evidence is small-sample.
Nimmo and Langford start despite rest suggestions.
Watch Josh Hader and Bryan Abreu late; both are available and rested.

briefings.headline: deGrom attacks the heart; keep Alvarez off the barrel
briefings.message: Jacob deGrom starts. Work Yordan Alvarez carefully with offspeed away from the barrel; do not challenge him in the zone. Favor breaking balls to Isaac Paredes and keep Jeremy Peña’s breaking balls down. With a close late lead, the plan calls for Cole Winn, Tyler Alexander, then Jacob Latz; use the rested leverage arms by situation. Gray, Ahlstrom, and Peoples are available but secondary workload options.
reminders: deGrom’s planned limit is 95 pitches; expected outing is 6.0 innings.
Use breaking or offspeed to finish Taylor Trammell.
Save the closer for the highest-leverage finish when the scenario calls for it.
